title: Patient perspective on follow-up care for bladder cancer: experiences with cystoscopy and acceptance of AI-supported urine cytology
summary:
Background:
Cystoscopy plays a central role in both the diagnosis and follow-up of bladder cancer. However, this examination is invasive and is perceived as burdensome to varying degrees by patients. In addition, urine cytology represents a non-invasive alternative method in which cells from the urine are examined for tumor-related changes. However, the diagnostic accuracy of this method is limited, particularly for the detection of low-grade tumors, and strongly depends on the experience of the examiner. Therefore, research is currently being conducted on new and innovative approaches, such as the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to analyze urine tests, with the aim of making follow-up care less invasive in the future.

Research Question:
The aim of this study is to explore how patients experience cystoscopy and how burdensome they perceive the procedure to be. In addition, the study investigates how open patients are to new, non-invasive diagnostic approaches, such as urine tests analyzed by artificial intelligence. The results are intended to help better align ongoing research and, in the future, follow-up care for bladder cancer with the needs and preferences of patients.

Methods:
The study consists of a questionnaire-based survey distributed nationwide through the self-help groups of the German Bladder Cancer Self-Help Association (Selbsthilfe-Bund Blasenkrebs e.V.). Participants can complete the questionnaire either online or in paper form. Prior to participation, they receive a short introductory video, written study information, and an informed consent form. Completing the questionnaire takes approximately 20–30 minutes. There are no additional appointments or follow-up surveys. All data are collected anonymously and exclusively through the questionnaire.

interventions.name: Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of bladder cancer are surveyed once using a standardized questionnaire about their experiences with follow-up care (cystoscopy) and their attitudes toward new, non-invasive diagnostic alternatives, in particular AI-supported urine tests.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed diagnosis of bladder cancer, membership in a support group or contact through such a group, sufficient knowledge of German, capacity to give consent
Exclusion criteria:
Incapacity to give consent, insufficient knowledge of German, no diagnosis of bladder cancer
